evidence: The collection count in cw_replace_all_atomic is inconsistent: .qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r3/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:110 permits "at least four literal matches" but then requires "exactly the four intended replacements". Five or more matches are a permitted fixture; replacing the entire collection correctly violates the literal four-replacement bar. ui.md:11 asks for Replace all without a four-match limit. Functional prompt.md:5 allows choosing exact fixtures proving the stated behavior, so no prompt restricts this to exactly four. A second count mismatch is judge.toml:65: "at least two" selected lines but Undo/Redo readbacks say "both"; with three selected lines this does not clearly require validating all three during undo/redo. Other reviewed plural bars explicitly cover their full fixed collections (three carets/all fifteen characters at :74, all three Find matches at :92, every original occurrence/all Redo at :110, all saved fields and both editor roles in stale-save). Unchanged guards are scoped to source/near-match/saved head and allow intended edits, new restored revisions, status feedback and read-only history; no additional unchanged-side-effect defect found. This is source-semantic evidence, not a configured judge measurement.
counterexample: Conforming alternative: create five case-sensitive CW31 literals across lines plus cw31, replace all with ALT31, and atomically Undo/Redo. Correct output has five ALT31 replacements and unchanged cw31, but the stated "exactly ... four" bar can reject it. Plausible broken alternative: replace only four of those five matches; a literal four-replacement interpretation can accept the replacement-count leg despite one match remaining. For indentation, a three-line selection whose Tab affects all three but Undo/Redo updates only the first two can satisfy a readback limited to "both".
suggested_fix: Make fixture counts and whole-collection readbacks agree: use exactly four matches (or require all N observed matches) for Replace all, and require Undo/Redo to restore/reindent every selected line (or fix the selection to exactly two).
